# Published template source-fidelity audit, batch 5

Date: 2026-10-23

Audited Glass Pink, Golden Card, and Green Garden against every local capture manifest and the Chorlove source tree. All three canonical captures are `preview-frame.html` entries in `Chorlove/capture-manifest.json`; scanning all provider `capture-manifest.json` files found no other provider with these IDs. The archive contains server-rendered snapshots plus each page's compiled Next.js module, shared Chorlove CSS chunks, and captured assets. The exact page modules are `0wvjbn--75n3p.js` (Glass Pink), `00phb3uac959r.js` (Golden Card), and `0hs8-cen4~3dx.js` (Green Garden). The page modules preserve template-level interactions and animation values even though the full Next.js site runtime is not included in each isolated package; the adapters can therefore be compared against and derive from the original compiled behavior.

## Image behavior

- Glass Pink and Green Garden both have template-owned floral opening/decorative images, which remain part of the design and appear in their current first-page previews. Their captured gallery slots point to `/images/templates/orchid-amplop/gallery-*.webp`, which are cross-template Orchid-Amplop sample photos, not authentic assets of these two templates. They remain excluded; these captures contain no attributable template-owned gallery photos to add as preview-only gallery content.
- Golden Card's capture contains template-owned mandala/corner art and no gallery photos. Its authentic cover keeps that ornamental opening visible.
- The shared fixture's six gallery entries currently have empty image URLs. Glass Pink hides the photo/story section when both story chapters and usable gallery images are absent; Green Garden hides its gallery section when there are no gallery image sources. Public display therefore has no default sample photos. Golden Card has no source gallery-photo slot in its captured snapshot.
- Product rule: when template-owned source gallery photos do exist, use them only in catalog and initial template-selection previews, ephemerally. Creator uploads replace preview samples when present. Public invitations hide optional creator-photo galleries until the creator uploads at least one image. This does not hide source-owned opening artwork, backgrounds, ornaments, or other template decoration.

## Shared contract and interaction review

The staged bridges contain app-level mappings for invitation content, language, RSVP, guest wishes, venue/map and calendar controls, gallery, music, and gift card details where represented. Glass Pink and Green Garden explicitly gate their gift sections on `toyona.enabled` and fill the card number/holder from the shared contract. The static HTML captures cannot establish original source-side handlers, music behavior, or animation timing. The app adapters implement the interactive opening and service wiring; reduced-motion paths are present in their CSS/JavaScript (including `prefers-reduced-motion`). The template-local CSS and locally packaged assets keep the captured ornamental styles/fonts available; the remaining references to Chorlove utility styles are served from the shared local package. Green Garden's package notes three archive-referenced decorative images as missing from the capture; its adapter currently excludes them rather than substituting unrelated art.

New image rule from the user: use authentic, template-owned source images in catalog and initial template-selection previews wherever available. Keep those preview-only and ephemeral; never persist them in a draft or public invitation. Creator-uploaded photos replace preview samples, and public photo galleries stay hidden until an upload exists. Template-owned opening/decorative artwork continues to render when the gallery is empty. Avoid unrelated cross-template/source-site sample photos. This supersedes the earlier blanket instruction to leave all six preview gallery image URLs empty. The three repair tasks were updated to inspect source image availability and verify preview/public data separation.

## Focused verification

- `node --check` passed for Glass Pink `bridge.js` and `source-adapter.js`, Golden Card `bridge.js`, and Green Garden `bridge.js`.
- `node --test tests/glass-pink-template.test.ts tests/golden-card-template.test.ts tests/green-garden-template.test.ts` did not complete cleanly. Glass Pink and Golden Card could not import the unlinked workspace module `@taklifnoma/contracts`. Green Garden ran: 3 checks passed, 2 failed (staged snapshot hash and stale shared-fixture hash). No dependency installation was attempted.
- Image dimensions and checksums were read from the local artifacts; visual review confirmed the screenshot UI described above. The source archive was not modified.

## Repair tasks

Created separate Taklifnoma project tasks for Glass Pink, Golden Card, and Green Garden. Each task must preserve the archived source capture untouched, make the smallest source/art correction, update provenance and focused checks, and avoid changing publication state, event compatibility, deployment, or payments.

## Repair follow-up (2026-10-23)

- Golden Card's preserved `source/preview-frame.html` now matches the archive byte-for-byte; its full closed-card portrait remains appropriate.
- Green Garden's preserved snapshot and fixture provenance were corrected. Its current portrait cover is a clean render of the floral opening without app/browser controls.
- Glass Pink's fonts are packaged locally and its canonical snapshot is preserved. The catalog cover is now a 432×768 capture of the actual renderer iframe after the opening fonts loaded and finite reveal animations finished. Visual inspection confirms the full floral envelope with one title and one open action; the language picker, music toggle, Next.js badge, and scrollbar are excluded. Provenance records the canonical fixture and capture hashes. The cover is eligible for catalog use.
- The archived snapshots alone do not contain executable page behavior, but each original compiled page module is present in Chorlove's captured `_next/static/chunks/` tree. Those modules were inspected to compare and restore the source opener, hero entrance, particle, and parallax behavior in the isolated adapters. The app adapters remain a separate integration surface for invitation data, platform APIs, locales, and reduced motion. Green Garden's two source-referenced `leaf1-bloom.webp` ornaments remain unavailable in the full local archive; the package preserves their original markup and records the missing capture asset rather than substituting another template's artwork.
- Focused command `pnpm exec tsx --test tests/glass-pink-template.test.ts tests/golden-card-template.test.ts tests/green-garden-template.test.ts` passes 18/18 after this capture correction. Both Glass Pink bridge scripts pass `node --check`.
